loop.title: One loop from invisible to recommended.
loop.description: Visibility in AI-assisted shopping is not a brand metric. It is an operational loop, and ecentic runs all four steps for every product in your catalog.

steps.title: Simulate
steps.description: ecentic has ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini compare your products with real competitors', the way they would for a shopper.

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.description: See exactly which products agents skip, who they pick instead, and which missing attribute cost you the cart.

steps.title: Optimize
steps.description: ecentic rewrites the title, description and structured data. Click Apply and the fix goes to your store.

steps.title: Track
steps.description: Rescan after a fix to see how your win rate moved. On Shopify, watch the visits AI assistants send you, week over week.

items.title: Agent checkout (UCP)
items.description: On WooCommerce, the free ecentic plugin lets agents search, fill a cart and check out through UCP, and the order lands in your store. On Shopify, ecentic checks the Merchant Center settings Google's agent checkout needs.

items.title: Google Merchant Center sync
items.description: On Shopify, ecentic sends the fixes you publish to Merchant Center as a supplemental feed, so Google's AI Mode and Gemini read the same product data your store shows. It also flags Merchant Center issues and the settings agent checkout needs.

faqSection.title: Frequently asked questions
faqSection.description: Common questions from merchants evaluating AI ecommerce tools.

items.question: What makes AI ecommerce tools different from standard ecommerce software?
items.answer: AI ecommerce tools need to help merchants structure product data, explain why listings lose, and improve pages that AI shopping systems compare in seconds. That is different from a generic dashboard or a copy generator that only rewrites descriptions.

items.question: Does ecentic replace an ecommerce platform?
items.answer: No. ecentic sits on top of an existing store stack. It connects to the catalog, runs simulations against competitors, and helps merchants publish clearer listing updates back into the platform they already use.

items.question: Who should start with the features page first?
items.answer: Teams evaluating AI ecommerce tools, agent-commerce workflows, or product listing optimization usually start here because it explains the full simulation, diagnosis, and optimization loop before they choose a platform-specific path.

items.question: Which pages should merchants read next?
items.answer: Most merchants move from the features page to the AI product listing optimization page, then into a platform page such as Shopify or WooCommerce, and finally into comparison or blog content for deeper research.
